title: Lynx Data - privacy pilot call notes + integration sketch
content:
Context: quick user-scratchpad after 2025-11-07 call with Lynx Data (trialing private deployment for PHI-adjacent analytics). Account lead: Tom H. Primary contact: Nina O. Technical lead: Ravi S.

Call summary (informal):
- Lynx is a mid-size health analytics vendor, processing daily feeds of de-identified claims + flagged PII fields. They want LLM-assisted coding of anomalies and natural-language summarization for clinician dashboards.
- Primary blocker: compliance requires no plaintext PII leaving their VPC and prefer customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Secondary: strict 200ms p50 latency requirement for short completions (<128 tokens) on interactive workflows. Batch jobs (overnight) can be slower.
- They want a short pilot (4 weeks) to validate accuracy and SLOs, then discuss Dedicated pool or on-prem variant.

Technical notes / constraints:
- Data flow they propose: ETL -> sanitized staging -> redact/hashed identifiers -> LLM in private deployment -> results back to staging with audit trail.
- They asked about: KMS/HSM integration (bring-your-own-key), audit logs (per-request), and support for FIPS endpoints.
- Networking: VPC peering from their AWS account to Redwood Private control plane preferred. They asked about egress rules and whether we need an inbound NAT for agent polling.
- Model estate: they prefer an opt-in open model (LLAMA-variant) quantized to int8 to reduce GPU footprint. Concern: quantization quality for clinical terms.

Gotchas / risks we called out:
- Redaction pitfalls: naive redaction can break context and hurt quality — recommend prefix-based KV cache + policy to surface redaction tokens in results for traceability.
- KMS latency: if we call external KMS on every request signing, p50 will blow past 200ms. Need local HSM proxy or session keys.
- VPC peering + cross-account routing can introduce hiccups during failover — plan fallback to a dedicated hosted-model variant (non-PII safe) but they are hesitant.
- Annotation feedback loop: they want to sync human corrections back into their dataset; be explicit on data retention policy for pilot.

Requirements (customer stated / inferred):
- Must: Private deployment in their AWS VPC or on-prem air-gapped option.
- Must: Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and per-request audit logs retained for 90 days.
- Want: <200ms p50 for short interactive queries, 99th percentile within 1s.
- Want: Model explainability tokens (where model indicates which input tokens influenced output) or at least token-level scoring to help triage hallucinations.
- Nice-to-have: UI widgets in Redwood Console to mark bad outputs and trigger retrain/label jobs.

Quick integration sketch (ops + infra):
1) Network: set up VPC peering + private endpoints; use egress-only NAT in their subnet for control-plane calls.
2) Keys: deploy HSM proxy in their account that provides short-lived session keys to runtime; Redwood will cache session tokens for X mins to avoid per-request KMS calls.
3) Runtime: spin a small int8-quantized Llama-variant on 1x A10G-equivalent for pilot; enable KV prefix caching and 4-request batching window of 20ms adjustable.
4) Observability: enable token-level traces, cost-per-call breakdown, and redact raw inputs in logs (store hashes + metadata).

Open questions (need answers from Lynx):
- Can they accept session-key approach (we exchange long-lived credential during provisioning, they host HSM proxy that mints ephemeral keys)?
- Expected concurrent interactive users during pilot (est for capacity planning).
- Any regulatory form (BAA / DPA) already pre-signed? Which corporate contact owns it?

Action items and owners (rough):
- Tom: schedule 1hr infra deep-dive with their network/SRE (target week of 2025-11-17).
- Aisha (me): draft pilot runbook + data retention appendix (due 2025-11-10).
- Ravi: prototype KMS-proxy integration doc and latency test script (PoC run by 2025-11-21).
- Nina: send sample (redacted) payloads and concurrency expectations.

Risk mitigation recommendations (ops notes):
- Pre-warm model and pin weights to avoid first-token latency cliff on interactive flows.
- Use local session key cache with soft TTL ~10m to balance security and latency.
- Baseline quantization QA: run 200 example clinical prompts through int8 and fp16 to measure regression; if >6% accuracy drop, swap to fp16 or 4-bit only for specific layers.

Draft Slack snippet for #cs-lynx-data (paste-ready):
"Quick writeup from today's call w/ Lynx Data — they need private deploy + CMK/HSM + 200ms p50 interactive. Pilot scope: infra + model QA + audit logs. Tom to lead infra call. I'll share pilot runbook draft by 11/10.

Questions for team: has anyone done a HSM-proxy pattern with session-key caching in production? Trying to avoid synchronous KMS per-request."

Notes-to-self: keep this lean; Lynx cares a lot about traceability and determinism. Avoid promising hosted-fallback unless we can guarantee data never leaves their VPC.

Version history: created quick after call 2025-11-07, updated with follow-ups 2026-02-20 (added latency test plan and session-key sketch).

-- end of scratchpad --
